title: Mass Storage Structure
body:
The hardware under [[File Systems]]: disks, what makes them slow, and what the OS does
about it.

## Why a disk is not memory

A spinning disk has to physically move to reach your data, and the cost of an access is
almost entirely that movement:

| Component | What it is | Rough cost |
|---|---|---|
| Seek time | move the arm to the right track | milliseconds, the dominant term |
| Rotational latency | wait for the sector to come round | milliseconds |
| Transfer time | actually move the bytes | microseconds |

Seek dominates, and that single fact drives every decision below. Reading two blocks on one
track is enormously cheaper than reading two blocks on distant tracks, even though it is the
same number of bytes.

It is also the bottom rung of the hierarchy in [[Cache]]: registers, cache, [[Main memory]],
disk, each level roughly a hundred times slower and a hundred times bigger than the last.
Do not re-derive that table here.

## Disk scheduling

Because seeks dominate, the OS does not serve requests in arrival order. It keeps a queue
per disk and reorders it:

| Algorithm | Picks | Problem |
|---|---|---|
| FCFS | whatever asked first, [[FIFO]] | arm swings wildly across the disk |
| SSTF | the request closest to the current head position | requests at the edges can [[Starvation\|starve]] |
| SCAN (elevator) | sweep to one end serving everything, then sweep back | edges wait longer than the middle |
| C-SCAN | sweep one way only, then jump back to the start | fairer wait times, wasted return trip |

The same [[Fairness]]-against-throughput trade as [[CPU Scheduling]], with a physical arm
instead of a CPU. SSTF is shortest-job-first and starves for the same reason.

## What SSDs change

No arm, no rotation, so seek time disappears and the scheduling algorithms above stop
mattering much. What replaces them: writes must erase a whole block first, and blocks wear
out, so the drive remaps blocks underneath you to spread the damage. The OS's job shifts
from ordering seeks to not writing more than it has to.
